meaning:
ταπεινόω, -ῶ
(ταπεινός), [in LXX chiefly for עָנָה, also for שָׁפֵל, כָּנַע, etc. ;]
to make low: ὄρος (βουνόν), Luk.3:5 (LXX). Metaphorical, to humble, abase: Mat.18:4 23:12, Luk.14:11 18:14, 2Co.11:7 12:21, Php.2:8; pass., Mat.23:12, Luk.14:11 18:14, Php.4:12; id. with mid. sense, Jas.4:10, 1Pe.5:6.†
(AS)

elsewhere.note: Whoever therefore humbles himself as this little child is the greatest in the Kingdom of Heaven.
Every valley will be filled. Every mountain and hill will be brought low. The crooked will become straight, and the rough ways smooth.
Or did I commit a sin in humbling myself that you might be exalted, because I preached to you God’s Good News free of charge?
And being found in human form, he humbled himself, becoming obedient to the point of death, yes, the death of the cross.
Humble yourselves in the sight of the Lord, and he will exalt you.
Humble yourselves therefore under the mighty hand of God, that he may exalt you in due time,
